scalable.title: Scalable Architecture: Where to Start?
scalable.excerpt: Principles for designing systems that grow with your business.
scalable.author: Maryam Hosseini

content.p1: Scalability is one of the most important concerns of any technical team. In this article, we cover the fundamental principles of designing scalable systems.
content.p2: Each part of the system should have a clear responsibility. This principle is the foundation of microservices architecture and helps horizontal scalability.
content.p3: Using Redis or CDN can significantly reduce the load on the database. But do not forget the cache invalidation strategy.
content.p4: Without monitoring, you cannot tell where the bottleneck is. Take tools like Prometheus and Grafana seriously from day one.
content.quote: Scalability is not a feature; it is a mindset.

react.title: 10 Professional React Tips You Should Know
react.excerpt: From memoization to folder structure, tips that make your code cleaner.
react.author: Saeed Karimi

content.p1: React is a powerful tool, but using it correctly requires following patterns. In this article, we review 10 key tips.
content.p2: Not all components need memo. Only where frequent re-rendering is problematic.
content.p3: Many React bugs come from wrong dependency arrays. Use the ESLint plugin.
content.h3: 3. Keep State as Low as Possible
content.p4: Keep state in the closest component that needs it, not at the highest level.

devops.title: DevOps Culture: Beyond Tools
devops.excerpt: Why is DevOps a culture, not just a set of tools?
devops.author: Mohammad Sadeghi

content.p1: DevOps is first and foremost an organizational culture. Tools are just enablers.
content.h1: Collaboration Between Dev and Ops Teams
content.p2: Breaking down the wall between developers and the operations team is the first step.
content.p3: From testing to deployment, whatever can be automated should be.

data.title: Data-Driven Decision Making in Organizations
data.excerpt: How to turn data into actionable insights?
data.author: Amir Tehrani

content.p1: Data without analysis is just numbers. Data-driven decision making requires process and culture.
content.p2: Before any analysis, determine what question you want to answer.
content.p3: A dashboard should enable the decision-maker to act, not just display numbers.

security.title: Security from Day One: Why After Release is Too Late
security.excerpt: Secure design principles that must be followed from the start.
security.author: Zahra Nouri

content.p1: Adding security after release is like locking a door in a wall that doesn't exist.
content.p2: Each user and service should only have access to what it needs.
content.p3: Sensitive data must be encrypted both in transit and at rest.

ux.title: UX Principles Every Developer Should Know
ux.excerpt: Good design is the result of collaboration between designer and developer.
ux.author: Negar Ahmadi

content.p1: A developer who knows UX principles builds better products.
content.p2: Every user action should have immediate feedback to preserve the sense of control.
content.p3: Every extra element is a cognitive load. Simpler is better.
